interface.title: miRacle — Explainable miRNA candidate triage
interface.stage_of_work: computational triage before wet-lab validation (choosing which candidate loci to test first)
interface.what_it_is_for: Fold a short human DNA/RNA sequence with ViennaRNA, score its hairpins with a logistic-regression classifier, and show a ranked, explainable shortlist of pre-miRNA-like candidates with structure, feature sensitivity, matches to curated references and Rfam decoys, and machinery/literature evidence.

data.note: This run explored the Streamlit reference app at http://127.0.0.1:8501/. It did not explore the README's primary browser interface (Next.js/WASM). Most runs used the bundled controls: the MIR21 hg38 region chr17:59,840,773-59,841,772 (1,000 nt), the external MIR1225 DROSHA control loaded into the text box, and the Compare-controls pairs (MIR21 vs. Rfam snoRNA, MIR630 vs. Rfam tRNA). I uploaded one test file, nr_030359_mir630.fa (97 nt RNA). I also pasted one sequence of my own, a mir-155-like hairpin; the trace records it as 63 nt, although an earlier note said 96 nt with flanking bases. The Evaluation tab reads bundled metrics. A UCSC fetch for a coordinate range that is not bundled (chr15:72,495,000-72,495,800) failed because the server has no network. The replay loaded the bundled sub-region chr17:59,841,100-59,841,500 (401 nt) to test the protein-region masking modes.
